title: Development Economics Adventure 3: Sustainable Development
welcome_lead: Today you'll weigh growth against sustainability and meet the UN SDGs.

final_note: You discussed sustainable development pathways and the role of SDGs.

walkthroughs.body_html:
UN Brundtland Commission (1987): development that meets the needs of the present without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their own.

Three pillars: economic, social, environmental.

Weak sustainability (Solow, Hartwick): manufactured capital can substitute for natural capital — drill the oil if you invest the proceeds.

Strong sustainability (Daly): some natural capital (atmosphere, biodiversity) is non-substitutable and must be preserved.

Tools: Pigouvian taxes, cap-and-trade, biodiversity offsets, green GDP.

UN SDGs (2015): 17 goals from no poverty to climate action by 2030.

Johan Rockström (2009): nine planetary boundaries, of which several (climate, biodiversity, nitrogen) are already breached.

Kate Raworth (2017) framed development as the 'doughnut' — between social floor and ecological ceiling.
